turns.en: Here's your medication to take home. One in the morning, one at night, with food. Your follow-up letter will come in the post. Any questions before you go?
turns.cy: Dyma'ch moddion chi i fynd adra. Un yn y bore, un gyda'r nos, efo bwyd. Mi ddaw'ch llythyr dilynol chi drwy'r post. Unrhyw gwestiynau cyn i chi fynd?
chunks: Here's your medication to take home
Dyma'ch moddion chi i fynd adra
English's 'take home' becomes a bare going-verb — the medicine goes, it is not taken
One in the morning, one at night, with food
Un yn y bore, un gyda'r nos, efo bwyd
Welsh marks evening with gyda'r nos, which English's 'at night' does not distinguish
Your follow-up letter will come in the post
Mi ddaw'ch llythyr dilynol chi drwy'r post
the post is drwy in Welsh, not yn
Unrhyw gwestiynau cyn i chi fynd?

turns.en: Hang on, let me write this down. One in the morning, one at night, with food. Got it.
turns.cy: Arhoswch funud — gadwch i mi sgwennu hyn i lawr. Un yn y bore, un gyda'r nos, efo bwyd. Dallt.
chunks: English's particle verb has no Welsh reflex — 'wait a minute' carries it
gadwch i mi sgwennu hyn i lawr
One in the morning, one at night, with food
Un yn y bore, un gyda'r nos, efo bwyd
one form for the ratifying intention, as at 'Understood'

turns.en: Perfect. And the district nurse will call on Thursday to check the dressing - you don't need to do anything, she'll just come to the house.
turns.cy: Perffaith. Ac mi ddaw'r nyrs ardal ddydd Iau i tsiecio'r rhwymyn — does dim angen i chi wneud dim byd, mi ddaw hi i'r tŷ.
chunks: And the district nurse will call on Thursday
Ac mi ddaw'r nyrs ardal ddydd Iau
English's 'call' for a home visit relocates to plain dod; the day takes the adverbial mutation
you don't need to do anything
does dim angen i chi wneud dim byd
'anything' under negation → dim byd; the negative existential need-frame
she'll just come to the house
'just' erased — the plain future carries it

turns.en: Thursday, the nurse. I'll put this note on the fridge.
turns.cy: Dydd Iau, y nyrs. Mi ro i'r nodyn 'ma ar yr oergell.
chunks: I'll put this note on the fridge
Mi ro i'r nodyn 'ma ar yr oergell

turns.en: Right then, Mrs Hughes, you take care of yourself. And nothing heavier than the kettle for two weeks.
turns.cy: Reit 'ta, Mrs Hughes — cymrwch ofal ohonoch chi'ch hun. A dim byd trymach na'r tegell am bythefnos.
chunks: English's ambiguous 'you take' is an imperative here; Welsh must choose, and the conjugated ohonoch carries 'of'
And nothing heavier than the kettle for two weeks
A dim byd trymach na'r tegell am bythefnos
pythefnos is one word for 'two weeks' — Welsh counts fortnights

turns.en: The kettle I can live with. Thank you for everything, all of you.
turns.cy: Mi fedra i fyw efo'r tegell. Diolch am bob dim, bob un ohonoch chi.
chunks: The kettle I can live with
Mi fedra i fyw efo'r tegell
English's fronted object cannot front in Welsh without a cleft — the plain order carries it instead

turns.en: Here's your medication. One in the morning, one at night, with food. Any questions?
turns.cy: Dyma'ch moddion chi. Un yn y bore, un gyda'r nos, efo bwyd. Unrhyw gwestiynau?
chunks: One in the morning, one at night, with food
Un yn y bore, un gyda'r nos, efo bwyd

turns.en: What happens if I forget a dose? Do I take two the next time?
turns.cy: Be sy'n digwydd os dw i'n anghofio dos? Ydw i'n cymryd dau y tro nesa?
chunks: What happens if I forget a dose?
Be sy'n digwydd os dw i'n anghofio dos?
the sy'-focus interrogative; the Welsh present covers English's future-in-if
Do I take two the next time?
Ydw i'n cymryd dau y tro nesa?

turns.en: If you forget, just take the next one at the normal time. Never double up. There's a leaflet in the box that says the same.
turns.cy: Os anghofiwch chi, cymrwch yr un nesa ar yr amser arferol. Peidiwch byth â dyblu. Mae 'na daflen yn y bocs sy'n deud yr un peth.
chunks: the short future in the if-clause, where English uses a present
just take the next one at the normal time
cymrwch yr un nesa ar yr amser arferol
English's bare 'never' relocates to the peidiwch â negative imperative with byth inside it
There's a leaflet in the box that says the same
Mae 'na daflen yn y bocs sy'n deud yr un peth
the mae 'na existential with a sy'-relative

turns.en: Never double up. Right. I'll put the leaflet somewhere safe.
turns.cy: Peidio byth â dyblu. Reit. Mi ro i'r daflen yn rhywle saff.
chunks: the patient reports the instruction, so the imperative becomes a verbal noun — Welsh cannot echo an imperative as English does
I'll put the leaflet somewhere safe
Mi ro i'r daflen yn rhywle saff

turns.en: Good. And the follow-up letter comes in the post - ring us if it's not here within two weeks.
turns.cy: Da iawn. Ac mi ddaw'r llythyr dilynol drwy'r post — ffoniwch ni os nad ydy o yma o fewn pythefnos.
chunks: And the follow-up letter comes in the post
Ac mi ddaw'r llythyr dilynol drwy'r post
ring us if it's not here within two weeks
ffoniwch ni os nad ydy o yma o fewn pythefnos
ffonio for telephoning, kept apart from canu for ringing a bell

turns.en: Will do. Thank you for everything.
turns.cy: Mi wna i. Diolch am bob dim.
chunks: English's subjectless ellipsis has no Welsh reflex — the subject must return

turns.en: Here's your medication and your discharge sheet. Any questions before you go?
turns.cy: Dyma'ch moddion chi a'ch taflen ryddhau. Unrhyw gwestiynau cyn i chi fynd?
chunks: Here's your medication and your discharge sheet
Dyma'ch moddion chi a'ch taflen ryddhau
⚠ line — taflen is feminine, so rhyddhau soft-mutates after it
Unrhyw gwestiynau cyn i chi fynd?

turns.en: Who do I ring if something goes wrong over the weekend?
turns.cy: Pwy dw i'n ei ffonio os eith rhywbeth o'i le dros y penwythnos?
chunks: ⚠ line — the resumptive ei after a fronted interrogative
if something goes wrong over the weekend?
os eith rhywbeth o'i le dros y penwythnos?
⚠ line — mynd o'i le is the fixed go-wrong idiom

turns.en: It's all on this sheet, look. The ward number's here, your GP, and 111 for out of hours. If it's chest pain or you can't breathe, it's 999 - no hesitating.
turns.cy: Mae'r cwbl ar y daflen 'ma, ylwch. Mae rhif y ward yn fan'ma, eich meddyg teulu chi, a 111 y tu allan i oriau. Os ydy hi'n boen yn y frest neu os fedrwch chi ddim anadlu, 999 amdani — dim oedi.
chunks: It's all on this sheet, look
Mae'r cwbl ar y daflen 'ma, ylwch
The ward number's here, your GP, and 111 for out of hours
Mae rhif y ward yn fan'ma, eich meddyg teulu chi, a 111 y tu allan i oriau
⚠ line — meddyg teulu is what a Welsh speaker says, not the initialism
If it's chest pain or you can't breathe
Os ydy hi'n boen yn y frest neu os fedrwch chi ddim anadlu
⚠ line — poen feminine (R8), so hi and y boen; the os must be restated on the second clause
⚠ line — the amdani ratifier does the work of English's 'it's'; 'no hesitating' becomes a bare verbal noun

turns.en: 999, no hesitating. My husband will remember that even if I don't.
turns.cy: 999, dim oedi. Mi fydd fy ngŵr i'n cofio hynna hyd yn oed os na fydda i.
chunks: My husband will remember that even if I don't
Mi fydd fy ngŵr i'n cofio hynna hyd yn oed os na fydda i
English's dummy 'don't' has no Welsh reflex — the negative future verb must be restated

turns.en: Put the sheet somewhere you'll both see it. And you've done really well - off you go home now.
turns.cy: Rhowch y daflen yn rhywle y gwelwch chi'ch dau hi. Ac rydach chi wedi gneud yn dda iawn — ffwrdd â chi adra rŵan.
chunks: Put the sheet somewhere you'll both see it
Rhowch y daflen yn rhywle y gwelwch chi'ch dau hi

⚠ line — 'both' forks by gender (S3); pinned MASCULINE here — the pair is the patient and her husband, and Welsh takes dau for a mixed pair; the same English chunk took dwy at SC01-F06-S05 where the pair was mother and daughter. Different worlds, different knowns — see §3
Ac rydach chi wedi gneud yn dda iawn

turns.en: The fridge, where everything important goes. Goodbye now, and thank you.
turns.cy: Yr oergell, lle mae bob dim pwysig yn mynd. Hwyl rŵan, a diolch.
chunks: The fridge, where everything important goes
Yr oergell, lle mae bob dim pwysig yn mynd
